      • checkOverflow

        public static void checkOverflow(int required,
                                 byte[] buffer,
                                 int offset)
                          throws BufferOverflowException
        Check that the required number of bytes are present in the array, starting from the provided offset. If not, throw a BufferOverflowException.
        Parameters:
        required - The number of bytes we expect to write
        buffer - The buffer to check
        offset - The offset to start from
        Throws:
        BufferOverflowException

      • checkUnderflow

        public static void checkUnderflow(int required,
                                  byte[] buffer,
                                  int offset)
        Check that the required number of bytes are present in the array, starting from the provided offset. If not, throw a BufferUnderflowException.
        Parameters:
        required - The number of bytes we expect to read
        buffer - The buffer to check
        offset - The offset to start from

      • putByteArray

        public static void putByteArray(byte[] value,
                                byte[] buffer,
                                int offset)
                         throws BufferOverflowException
        Copies the provided byte[] value into the buffer starting from the specified offset. Checks to ensure there is enough room to write into first, throwing a BufferOverflowException if there is not.
        Parameters:
        value - The byte[] to write into the buffer
        buffer - The buffer to write into
        offset - The offset to commence at
        Throws:
        BufferOverflowException - If there is not enough space to write the value into

      • readByteArray

        public static byte[] readByteArray(byte[] buffer,
                                   int offset,
                                   int length)
        Reads and returns a sub-byte[] from the given buffer. Starting at the offset position and extending for length bytes. If there is not enough information in the buffer to satisfy the request, a BufferUnderflowException is thrown.
        Parameters:
        buffer - The buffer to read from
        offset - The position to start reading from
        length - The number of bytes to read
        Returns:
        A new byte[] representing the sub-view of the buffer

      • putFloatBE

        public static void putFloatBE(float value,
                              byte[] buffer,
                              int offset)
        Write the given float value into the buffer, starting at the offset value.

        If there are less than 4 bytes from the offset to the length of the array, a BufferOverflowException will be thrown for the buffer overflow.
